Shelves of amber jars hold cloudy eyes and suspended teeth; dried bats hang from rafters beside bundled wormwood; a toad sits warming itself on a candle-scorched grimoire.
Roots crack through flagstone floor; fox skulls grin from every windowsill; a cauldron of dark broth steams; the walls are hidden entirely behind pinned moth-wings and handwritten curses.
Bundled herbs and crow feathers droop from every ceiling beam; a cracked black mirror reflects a room slightly different from this one; wax has pooled deep across the hearthstone.
Rows of tiny labelled drawers cover the eastern wall — WOLF TOOTH, RIVER GRIEF, CHILD'S FIRST LIE — each sealed with red wax and a pressed finger-mark.
A jar of bottled lightning pulses faint blue on the top shelf; below it, poppets hang by their necks; below those, a cat sleeps inside a human skull.
Pale fungi cluster along the skirting boards, softly luminous; pinned anatomical charts curl at every corner; a raven on a perch turns its head to watch you enter.
The table is buried under mortars, spilled salt circles, half-finished poppets, and a bird-cage full of articulated finger-bones wired into the shape of something that almost had wings.
Candle-stubs of every height line the mantelpiece, wax cascading into frozen rivers; above them, a garland of dried apples, rabbit skulls, and small clay faces no one has named.
Beeswax candles burn amber in every alcove; the ceiling is smoked dark from decades of incense; a glass dome on the dresser contains a tiny figure that occasionally moves.
Strings of yellowed teeth loop between shelves; a taxidermied stoat wears a crown of thorns; the floor is soft with scattered herbs — rosemary, rue, something unidentifiable and sweetly rotten.
A great leather-bound book lies open, its pages covered in red marginalia and pressed moth-wings; beside it, a bowl of dark water holds a reflection of an entirely different house.
The walls are furred with hanging roots and dried flower-heads; seven iron keys of different sizes dangle from one nail; a goat skull on the door-post has fresh milk in its eye-sockets.
Dozens of small bottled storms line the highest shelf, each one churning with internal weather — miniature lightning, thumbnail blizzards, one small bottle full of still and total dark.
A cracked apothecary cabinet crowds one wall, its hundred tiny drawers each labelled in faded ink; three drawers hang open, spilling dried black petals across the floor like a small disaster.
The spinning wheel in the corner is strung not with wool but with something translucent and faintly iridescent; a crow's nest built into the rafters holds three unblinking glass eyes.
Bookshelves lean at violent angles, books stacked horizontally, vertically, and on top of each other; a jar of preserved hands sits between a candelabra and a sleeping hedgehog.
Green moss creeps up the hearthside wall; the cauldron bubbles a deep umber; above the fireplace hangs a portrait of a woman who has been painted over four distinct times.
Every surface holds a jar — clouded vinegar with floating things, honey gone dark, oil with a suspended feather — all warm in the low light, all quietly, faintly breathing.
Wax-sealed letters addressed to no one are pinned across the ceiling with iron nails; below them, the table holds a dissected clock, three candles, and a cup of cold black something.
Animal skulls of every size line the highest shelf — mouse to horse — each filled with a burning tea-light, so the whole wall flickers with warm light behind hollow eyes.
A great stuffed owl presides over the room from the top of the wardrobe; its stomach has been opened and filled with folded paper charms; its glass eyes catch every candle.
The floor near the hearth has gone soft with spilled wax, fallen petals, scattered soil; something is growing up through the flagstones that looks like a hand made entirely of root.
Hundreds of small mirrors of every shape cover the north wall; none of them agree on what they are reflecting; the largest one is filled with a dark that has texture.
A cauldron steams faintly on the hearth; a black cat watches from the mantelpiece; the shelves behind hold nothing but jars, every jar holding something that used to be something else.
Dried roses, vertebrae, and crumpled star-charts hang from hooks in no apparent order; the amber glow of tallow candles makes everything look preserved, warm, faintly dangerous, and very old.
Shelves of amber jars hold floating eyes, curled embryos, shed skins; below, a cauldron breathes steam; above, a crow skull wears a crown of dried rue.
Walls papered with star-charts and pressed moths, every surface colonised by candle-stubs, fungal growth, bundled wormwood, a black mirror reflecting a room that isn't this one.
Hundreds of tiny labelled drawers climb the curved wall; between them, poppets hang by their ankles, stitched mouths whispering; a tallow candle gutters in a jawbone holder.
Roots have pushed through the flagstone floor, cradling fallen acorns and old coins; above them, dried hares dangle from the rafters, glassy-eyed, their fur still soft.
A worktable buried under open grimoires, spilled wax, and beetle-wing vials; a rat skeleton posed mid-stride on a velvet cushion; smoke curling from a clay censer.
Bottled storms line the highest shelf, lightning flickering behind green glass; below them, strings of wolf teeth and rowan berries loop between iron hooks like strange garlands.
The hearth is enormous and blackened, a pot of dark liquid simmering; bundles of mugwort, foxglove, and nightshade hang above it, slowly drying in the rising heat.
A taxidermied fox sits sentinel on the armchair, wearing a child's silver locket; around it, candle-drip has built stalactites of wax across the armrest over many years.
Jars of preserved hands, a dish of river-smooth stones each marked with a single rune, a weasel skull nested in black feathers — every inch a deliberate accumulation.
Fungi bloom in the corner where the wall is damp, phosphorescent and pale; shelves of coloured powders in twists of paper; a mortar stained seven shades of brown.
A birdcage holds no bird — only a floating blue flame and three keys; outside it, chains of finger-bones and amber beads curtain the doorway to an inner room.
The ceiling is low and hung with hundreds of dried flower bunches, seed-pods, and snakeskins; amber candlelight turns everything gold, casting long shadows of dangling roots across the walls.
Open books everywhere, their margins annotated in brown ink beside small pressed insects; between them, vials of iridescent liquid, a bowl of ash, a single black feather upright.
A great owl — stuffed, enormous — watches from the top of a wardrobe whose doors won't close over its contents: folded pelts, stoppered horns, a jar with something breathing.
Wax dolls with real hair pinned through them stand in a row along the sill; behind them, fogged glass shows only darkness, though no one has boarded the window.
The floor is soft with old rushes, herbs crushed underfoot releasing sage and iron; a pestle lies on its side, a rivulet of dark paste still oozing from it.
Stacks of handwritten recipe-books, their spines cracked, their pages stiff with ancient spillage; a black cat's skull bookends them beside a jar of preserved blackberries floating in something dark.
Animal skulls crowd the mantle — badger, deer, fox, something unidentifiable — each holding a tea-light; the heat makes the room smell of singed bone and old beeswax constantly.
Chains of dried mushrooms swag between shelves crowded with clay pots, labelled in a cramped hand: FORGETTING, BINDING, GRIEF, HUNGER; one pot has been sealed with red cord.
A spinning wheel threaded with something that isn't wool stands in the corner, humming faintly; around its base, a ring of salt and three offerings: a tooth, a coin, a feather.
Green glass bottles of every size catch the firelight; inside some, herbs, inside others, folded papers with names on them; the lowest shelf holds a jar simply labelled DO NOT.
The worktable is a landscape: pooled wax, scattered bone dice, a lodestone wrapped in red thread, ink wells, a half-assembled poppet splayed open, waiting for its heart of thistle.
A large mirror, face-down, wrapped in black cloth and tied with nine knots, propped against the wall; around it, protective chalk marks, burned-out candles, and a circle of iron nails.

Hundreds of tiny paper parcels hang from the ceiling on black threads, each knotted, each labelled; between them float softly glowing motes, circling without purpose, like thoughts let loose at night.
The room smells of earth, beeswax, old paper, copper, and something green and living; everything overlaps — jar on book on skull on cloth — a sediment of years of strange work.
Shelves of amber jars hold pickled eyes, floating moths, a preserved hand mid-gesture. Dried yarrow bundles brush the ceiling. A black cat sleeps between two skulls.
A cauldron bubbles green-gold over low embers. Roots push through flagstones. Every wall drawer bears a tiny inked label: CROW TONGUE, SLEEPSTONE, BORROWED BREATH.
Wax drips down every surface in long stalactites. Poppets hang by threads from roof beams, each stitched with someone's hair. A storm thrashes inside a corked bottle.
The black mirror reflects a room slightly different from this one. Moth wings pressed under glass. Shelves bowing under the weight of leaning, leather-spined books.
Taxidermied foxes wear tiny crowns. A cracked egg sits in a velvet nest, glowing faintly. Strings of teeth loop between iron hooks along the low-beamed ceiling.
Charts of stars curl from walls, annotated in cramped red ink. A mortar holds something still grinding itself. Fungi bloom orange and gold along the lowest shelf.
Forty candle-stubs burn at once, none the same height. A raven skull wears a ring. Bottled smoke drifts in lazy spirals inside a wax-sealed green flask.
Roots thick as wrists have split the hearthstone. Dried roses hang black overhead. A cloth doll in the corner turns its head when no one is watching.
Jars labelled SECOND SIGHT, WOLF HOUR, UNNAMED GRIEF line three shelves. Candlelight wavers across a cat spine strung like a necklace over the door lintel.
A spinning wheel threads silver through something unspooling from a jar. The floor is uneven earthen tile. Heaped amber beads and carved bone charms crowd every surface.
Pressed leaves cover one entire wall, pinned and annotated. Three iron cauldrons nest inside each other. A glass dome houses a tiny skeleton in a chair, posed reading.
Green mold traces veins up the stone wall like a second map. Wax effigies stand in rows. The room smells of mushroom, iron, burned sugar, and old rain.
Animal skulls form a long windowsill procession: rabbit, fox, crow, something unnamed. Candles burn inside each eye socket. The ceiling is low and hung with braided garlic.
A trapdoor left ajar exhales cold air. Shelves overflow with rolled bark-scrolls. A hedgehog preserved in resin sits beside a clay bowl still wet with something dark.
The hearth is enormous and old, blackened with decades. Above it: a chart of moon-phases, blood-spotted. A goat skull center-mounted, garlanded with dried cornflowers and iron nails.
Every drawer knob is a different animal eye, glass and staring. Wax pools on manuscript pages. A pendulum swings without being touched, above a bowl of still black water.
Acorns, antlers, and snake vertebrae fill a wide wooden bowl. Jewel-tone bottles crowd the windowsill, throwing red and green light. Something inside one bottle presses against the glass.
Strings of drying mushrooms loop from beam to beam. A copper alembic sweats slow amber drops. Three poppets in the corner are tied back-to-back with red thread, grimacing.
A weasel in a jar floats alongside seven small teeth. The table holds a half-finished hex, feathers and pins arranged in a careful star. Ink still wet.
The ceiling is low enough to touch, crusted with candle-smoke and cobweb. Shelves hold stoppered bones. A living plant grows through a human jaw placed in soil.
Hundreds of tiny labelled drawers cover the far wall floor-to-ceiling. HORNET MEMORY. BLUE HOUR SALT. TEETH OF A LIAR. A stool sits before them, well-worn.
A lantern made from a ribcage throws barred golden light. Dried herbs crumble over open spell-pages. The cauldron's steam smells of pine, copper, and something like a name.
Candles planted directly in the earthen floor surround a chalk circle. On the shelves beyond: jars of feathers sorted by color, bird, season, and quality of death.
The window is small, deep-silled, and crowded with moss-covered bottles. Inside each bottle: folded paper, named. Ivy pushes through the gap. The candle here is never lit.
A carved wooden chair holds a bundled figure of rags and antler. Fox teeth hang from the arms. The fire in the hearth is older than anyone living.
Amber jars crowd every shelf — pickled eyes, coiled serpents, a preserved hand mid-gesture. Dried sage bundles brush the ceiling. A tallow candle gutters beside an open, annotated grimoire.
Roots have split the hearthstone and curl toward the fire. Poppets dangle from blackened rafters. A clay pot bubbles something green and faintly luminous, smelling of pine resin and copper.

Walls lined floor-to-ceiling with tiny labelled drawers: WOLF TEETH, BORROWED BREATH, THURSDAY DUST. A crow perches on a brass scales, watching. Wax has dripped into permanent amber pools across the floor.
A black mirror leans against foxed wallpaper, reflecting a room slightly different from this one. Bundles of dried rue and mugwort hang so thickly the ceiling seems to breathe.
The cauldron is iron-black and enormous, squatting over low coals. Something stirs inside it without a spoon. Skulls of fox, hare, and rook are arranged on the mantel with careful ceremony.
Charts of star-paths curl at their edges, pinned with bone needles to every vertical surface. A bottled storm flickers blue on the windowsill, sealed with seven knots of red thread.
Fungi — oyster-pale and bracket-brown — grow in tiers up one damp wall. Interspersed among them, tiny labelled jars glow amber and rose. A poppet stitched from burlap hangs watching from a nail.
Strings of teeth loop between shelves like garlands: human molars, fox canines, something longer and less identifiable. The fire is low but the room is close and warm with old smoke.
A taxidermied magpie perches mid-stride on a stack of water-stained herbals. Beside it, a jar of floating eyeballs all face one direction. The direction is toward you.
The floor is strewn with rush matting, herbs pressed flat underfoot, and the occasional clean-licked bone. Jars of honey glow gold among jars of darker, unnameable things on every crowded shelf.

Candle-stubs of every height colonise every flat surface, dripped into baroque formations. Between them: teeth, pins, folded paper packets, a small iron key, and a dish of something still moving slightly.
A loom in the corner holds half-finished cloth woven with symbols that shift when seen sidelong. Dried flowers — black with age — are plaited through the warp threads like an offering.
An enormous leather-bound book lies chained to the worktable. Around it: inkwells of red and brown, a quill cut from something large, and finger-bones arranged as if mid-counting.
The window is covered entirely by hanging bundles — herbs, bones, feathers, small cloth sachets stitched shut — filtering the outside to a warm, resinous green-gold darkness within.
Shelves of wax figures — some cracked, some wrapped in thread, one with a crown of mouse-skulls. Each has a scrap of paper tucked beneath it, names written in cramped handwriting.
The hearth is hung with iron hooks bearing pots of every size. Above them, smoke-darkened paper charms are nailed in overlapping layers, reaching back through what looks like decades of careful work.
A raven skull sits in a nest of red thread and dried rosehips, surrounded by coins of unfamiliar currency. The candlelight makes its empty socket seem to track movement in the room.

Moss carpets the north corner entirely, creeping up shelving and around jars without disturbing them. Among it, mushrooms cluster at the base of a clay figure half-buried and half-emerging from the floor.
A wardrobe stands open: inside, coats of feather and skin and woven grass; a shelf of stoppered bottles labelled SLEEP, FORGETTING, THREE HOURS HENCE; and a smell of cold air and beeswax.

Hundreds of small mirrors — hand-mirrors, shaving-mirrors, a great oval one — cover one wall completely, each turned at a different angle, multiplying the candlelight and the clutter into infinite amber repetition.

An iron birdcage holds no bird, but the door swings slowly with no draught. Around its base: shed feathers, cracked shells, a tiny bowl of something dark and semi-liquid, coins with holes bored through.

The workbench is deep in layered debris — wax, string, dried petals, scattered teeth, three open books simultaneously consulted. A mortar and pestle in the centre holds something still faintly steaming and smelling of iron.
Whole walls are shelved with bottles containing things suspended in murky amber fluid: a coiled umbilicus, a set of fingers, a cloud, a small ship in a bottle inside a bottle.
Paper packets everywhere — tucked behind jars, pinned to rafters, folded beneath the legs of furniture. Each is sealed with wax and labelled in a hand too small to read from this distance.

The room smells of tallow, turned earth, pine resin, something sweet and something spoiled. Every object has been placed with intent. Nothing here is accidental. The witch is not present. The witch is not far.
Shelves of amber jars — pickled eyes, coiled roots, a suspended hummingbird — line walls papered with star-charts, candle-stubs melted into skulls, dried herbs raining from low rafters.
A cauldron bubbles green-gold over hearthfire, surrounded by towers of wax-sealed crocks, crow feathers, a badger skull wearing a tiny crown of blackthorn.
Rows of tiny labelled drawers — MOLE TEETH, GRIEF, FIRST SNOW — floor-to-ceiling beside a cracked black mirror reflecting a room that isn't quite this one.
Roots have broken through the floorboards, curling around glass bottles. A poppet hangs from a beam, stitched mouth moving almost imperceptibly in the candlelight.
The ceiling is a tangle of drying nettles, foxglove, and something unidentifiable, wound through with strings of vertebrae and little tin bells that ring without wind.
An overstuffed chair wears a fox pelt draped over one arm; beside it, a three-legged stool holds a bowl of dark water and a single floating candle.
Taxidermied magpies perch along a crooked shelf above bottled storms — corked vials containing tiny churning clouds — and a stoppered jar labelled SOMEONE'S LOST YEAR.
A toad sits on a grimoire, unbothered. Around it: spilled ink, pressed moths pinned to the open pages, a ring of salt, burnt match-stubs, pawprints in wax.
Moss creeps up the stone wall behind the worktable, overtaking jars of bone-pale powder and amber resin, the whole wall glowing faintly green with bioluminescent growth.
Strings of teeth — animal, otherwise — drape between shelves crowded with nesting poppets, each smaller than the last, each stitched with a different sorrow in red thread.
The hearth is heaped with ash and charmed pebbles; above it hangs a massive drying rack of herbs, skulls, and a suspended eelskin covered in tiny written names.
Curling alchemical charts cover every inch of one wall, pinned under clusters of dried mushrooms, the ink old and foxed, margin-notes scrawled in three competing, arguing hands.
A fat black candle burns on a pewter dish surrounded by shed snakeskin, a crow's foot tied in red cord, and small clay figures mid-gesture in the wax-drip.
Fungi grow from a fallen book in the corner — orange, cupped, luminous — the mycelium threading up through a jar of teeth and across the warped floorboards.
Stoppered bottles crowd every surface, contents swimming in amber: feathers, knucklebones, a tiny key, what appears to be frozen laughter, a sealed vial of pure humming dark.
The door is barely visible behind hanging bundles — mugwort, bone-set, iron-weed — strips of written bark, a nailed horseshoe black with age, a warning in no known alphabet.
An ink-dark cat sleeps across the open grimoire, tail over several important passages, surrounded by wax-pooled candlesticks, cracked lenses, and a jar of slowly orbiting teeth.
Animal skulls line the window ledge, each filled with something: beeswax, pine resin, dark water, a small rolled paper. Candlelight warms the bone to amber and pearl.
The worktable is a ruin of industry — mortars of half-ground root, scattered seeds, a thumb-bone stylus, a half-stitched poppet, spilled black ink forming a shape like a hand.
Jars of preserved things glow amber on high shelves: berries, eyeballs, a tiny fist, words written on submerged paper, something that presses against the glass when unobserved.
Feathers of every size porcupine from a clay jug; beneath it, a spread of small cards inked with symbols, a ring of mushrooms drawn in ash, a shed antler.
The cauldron lid lifts an inch on its own, releasing a plume of cedarsmoke; around the hearthstone: pawprints in old wax, a rune of bent nails, scattered kingfisher bones.
A wall of small framed specimens — moth-wings, pressed hands, a flattened frog, hair braided around wire, a butterfly labeled DREAM — jostles with iron hooks hung with charm-bundles.
Beeswax pillars stand at every height, their drips freezing into faces, hands, small figures mid-scream. Between them: seed packets labeled in no season, coiled cord, a lodestone in a nest.
The floor itself is chalked with a vast diagram, worn and re-drawn, circling the hearthstone — roots threading through it, a knocked-over salt-cellar, a footprint that points the wrong way.
Shelves of amber jars holding suspended eyes, crow feathers, and labelled teeth crowd walls where dried herbs hang in thick bundles above a low bubbling cauldron ringed by tallow-stubs.
A black mirror leans against shelves of bottled storms, its surface showing something that isn't the room; poppets dangle from the rafters on strings of knotted hair.
Roots have broken through the flagstone floor and curled around the chair legs; a fox skull wears a crown of dried cornflowers and holds a tallow candle in its jaws.
Hundreds of tiny labelled drawers cover the east wall floor to ceiling; one hangs open spilling dark soil and small bones; a moth rests on the brass handle, unmoving.
The cauldron breathes green-tinged steam into rafters hung with bat wings, herb bundles, and wasp nests; beeswax candles melt over stacked grimoires their pages marked with pressed nightshade.
A crow sits atop a glass dome housing a tiny preserved hand posed as if beckoning; below, jars of floating things glow faintly amber in the low candlelight.
Pelts and dried snakeskins drape over a chair buried under charts covered in cramped handwriting; the rug is moss and the moss is still growing up toward the windowsill.
Strings of teeth and dried berries loop between shelves where clay poppets stand in rows, each stitched with a different expression; one has been turned to face the wall.
A taxidermied hare in a velvet coat holds a burnt-down candle; behind it rises a wall of corked bottles containing what look like small weather systems, faintly lit from within.
Bundles of roots and wormwood hang so thick they form a second ceiling; below, the workbench holds an open skull, three inkwells, and a bowl of still-warm dark liquid.
The shelves sag under the weight of labelled jars — crow eyes, river mud, coiled shed skins — and a single jar at the end holds something that occasionally taps the glass.
Fungi grow in jewel tones along the baseboards and climb the legs of a wardrobe stuffed with folded papers, pouches of ash, and one child's wooden shoe, very old.
A mummified cat is curled on a stack of vellum charts mapping coastlines that don't exist; above it, a chandelier of antlers holds sixteen guttering candles at uneven heights.
Wax seals dozens of jars arranged by colour along a warped shelf; red ones contain petals and teeth; the black ones are turned backward so their labels face the wall.
A boar skull hangs beside a framed hornbook painted over with a different alphabet; below, a mortar stained dark purple sits among loose roots and a spilled chain of vertebrae.
The floor is barely visible beneath stacked crocks, rolled charts, and a sleeping black cat on a folded ritual cloth embroidered with moons; a kettle steams above a low peat fire.
Seed packets and stitched poppets pin hand-lettered notes to every surface; the notes are instructions or warnings, it's unclear; a green candle has melted entirely over a closed book.
A tall apothecary cabinet looms, its hundred drawers all slightly open, each one breathing its own smell — resin, sulphur, old blood, something floral — into the warm and crowded room.
Ribbons of dried entrail and silver thread hang alongside bundles of mugwort; a small iron cauldron holds a floating candle and three small stones that hum at different pitches.
Amber jars crowd every sill, some containing beetles suspended mid-flight; the spinning wheel in the corner spins on its own, the yarn it makes a deep and lightless red.
Shelves overflow with labelled skulls, glass eyes, coiled shed snake skins, and one jar marked GRIEF, its interior permanently fogged; a crow feather quill rests in an inkwell of rust.
An open grimoire holds a pressed luna moth between pages dense with recipe and curse; across the room its twin hangs live and still against a jar of goldenly glowing fat.
The ceiling is entirely obscured by hanging bundles — lavender, rue, finger bones, small tied figures — so thick that walking through disturbs them and they whisper against each other like breath.
A great iron pot hangs over embers in a sooted hearth flanked by jars of rendered fat and coiled roots; above the mantle a mirror shows last night's moon, not tonight's.

Every horizontal surface drowns in accumulation — tallow, bone, folded paper, sealed clay, dried fruit, labelled poison, curious tool — and one stool at the workbench still holds the shape of someone recently risen.
Shelves of stoppered jars hold cloudy eyes and pickled moth-wings; dried foxglove bundles hang from smoke-black rafters; a tallow candle gutters over a cracked skull stuffed with acorns.
Rows of tiny labelled drawers crowd the curved wall — TEETH OF LIARS, SLEEP TAKEN FROM CHILDREN, WET EARTH FROM THREE GRAVES — handles worn smooth by years of searching fingers.
A black mirror leans against bundled roots; before it, a dish of milk gone thick and yellow; something moves in the reflection that does not match the room.
Copper pots and clay crocks cluster the hearth-shelf, crusted with old spillings; a cauldron breathes slow green steam; the ladle has been carved from a single femur, handle-end a knuckle.
Poppets hang by their necks from an iron rod — rag-stuffed, button-eyed, each stitched with a name in thread the colour of old rust; one is newer than the others.
Fungi bloom from a split floorboard, amber-orange, fanning wide; around them, chalk figures have been drawn and then scrubbed and redrawn; wax pools have hardened into strange faces in the cracks.
A taxidermied crow sits atop a tower of almanacs, one glass eye replaced with a garnet; its wings are pinned open, small scrolls bound to each primary feather with red thread.
Strings of teeth loop between ceiling joists — animal and otherwise — glass beads threaded between each, amber and bone-white; they click softly with no draft to explain it.

The table is barely visible under rolled charts, a cracked astrolabe, three mortars with their pestles missing, a plate of gnawed bread, wax-sealed letters, and a glass bottle containing a tiny storm.
Jars of preserved toads line the window ledge, each posed differently — sitting, leaping, mouths gaping — the greenish preserving fluid lit gold by a single candle stub burning behind them.
A wardrobe stands open, spilling: cloaks the colour of mossed stone, belts of plaited hair, small bones sewn into hems, a hat with something living tucked inside the crown, quietly shifting.
Root-tips break through the plaster wall, dark and questing; someone has tied tiny knotted threads to each tip and labelled them in faded ink; the labels are names, not plants.
Bundles of drying herbs — mugwort, yarrow, nettle, things without common names — hang so thick the ceiling is invisible; their mingled reek is green and sharp and faintly animal.
A spinning wheel in the corner trails thread that fades from flax-gold to shadow-black; the bobbin is wound with what looks like hair; the wheel moves a quarter-turn without being touched.
Wax figures crowd a low shelf — churches, animals, a hanged man, a sleeping child — each studded with pins at specific angles, each sitting in its own dried ring of blood.
Books shelved spine-to-wall, titles inked onto pages visible: AGREEMENTS MADE IN AUTUMN, THE HONOURABLE ART OF UNMAKING, WHAT THE OX KNOWS AT SLAUGHTER; one lies open, held flat by a stone hand.
A chipped enamel basin holds dark water and floating petals; above it, a convex mirror hung with crow feathers reflects the room back wrong — the candles burning upward, the shadows standing still.
Stoppered vials dangle on cords from a rafter, each containing a different colour of smoke; they are warm to the touch; one rattles softly and regularly, like something trying to remember breathing.
Animal skulls line the mantelpiece — fox, hare, horse, something with too many eye-sockets — each filled with small offerings: salt, pins, crushed violets, teeth, a single dried blackthorn berry.
A worn armchair slumps before the hearth, its arms rubbed bare; on the side table: a cold cup, a half-eaten apple turning dark, a leather journal whose pages are slowly, steadily filling themselves.
Glass domes shelter preserved curiosities: a winged frog, a rose that moves when approached, a coiled snake swallowing a key, a small boy's shoe — empty but clearly still occupied by something.
The floor is flagstone and moss and thick with old candle-drippings shaped into a path that leads nowhere obvious, but everything in the room seems oriented subtly toward the same dark corner.
Three cauldrons, small to large: one holds bones bubbling clean, one holds something red and fragrant, one holds nothing visible but produces a low continuous hum felt more in the chest than heard.
A telescope aimed at the interior wall, not any window; chalked star-charts spread beneath it; at the eyepiece, a lens of polished obsidian; whatever it observes has been noted in cramped red ink.
Jars of honey — dark, almost black, something suspended in each one — stack in amber towers near the hearth; by firelight the suspended shapes in each jar seem to very slowly rotate.
Shelves of amber jars hold suspended eyeballs and tiny drowning moths; dried bundles of yarrow and blackthorn hang from every beam, brushing a visitor's hair.
A cauldron squats on hearthstones furred with moss, bubbling something greenish-gold; around it, animal skulls arranged in a spiral each bearing a lit tallow stub.
Walls papered entirely in overlapping star charts and anatomical drawings of unknown creatures; a black mirror propped in the corner reflects a room that isn't this one.
Hundreds of tiny labelled drawers cover one wall floor-to-ceiling, hand-lettered in faded ink: TEETH OF LIARS, CROW MEMORY, BORROWED LUCK, DREAM-SALT, HUSBAND'S TONGUE.
Poppets dangle from the rafters on knotted cord, their button eyes mismatched and watchful; one is dressed in a scrap of what appears to be a magistrate's coat.
Roots have broken through the floorboards entirely and curled around the chair legs, the table feet, the cauldron stand, as though the house is slowly being swallowed.
Jars of bottled storms line the mantelpiece — inside each, a tiny churning grey sky and the sound, if you lean close, of distant rain and something crying.
A writing desk buried under curling pages, feather quills, spilled black wax, a cracked hourglass, and a taxidermied raven mid-scream, holding a ring in its rigid claw.
Strings of yellowed teeth loop between nail-hooks across the ceiling like garlands; beneath them, bunches of dried fungi, black-spotted and velvet-capped, releasing faint sweet spores.
The hearth is enormous and ancient, stained with decades of smoke; hanging inside it, chains hold iron pots at different heights, each one murmuring with something alive.
A cabinet of curiosities covers an entire wall: foetal things in formaldehyde, pinned moth-wings beside human-shaped roots, a geode split to reveal a tiny furnished room inside.
Candle-stubs of every height crowd every flat surface, wax dripped into elaborate pale rivers and frozen pools; each flame burns a slightly different colour — amber, blue, green.
Books stacked so high they form columns supporting a second precarious shelf; between them, wedged tight, spell-bags of red thread and bone, smelling of iron and cloves.
A taxidermied fox sits upright in the best armchair wearing a small velvet collar; its glass eyes follow correctly. On the side table: a cooling cup of tea.
Moss grows thick across the north wall, threaded with pale bioluminescent fungi; carved into the plaster beneath, half-hidden by green growth, a calendar counting toward something unnamed.
A great loom in the corner threaded with hair — brown, silver, black, red — weaving itself slowly with no hands visible, producing cloth that shows faces in its pattern.
Shelves of bottled things: one contains a preserved hand still wearing a copper ring; one holds folded black feathers; one holds what appears to be a sleeping, breathing eye.
The floor is layered with overlapping rugs, each more worn than the last; between them, chalk circles and sigils, partially rubbed away, glowing faintly amber beneath the fringe.
A drying rack above the fire holds strips of something that is not quite meat; below, a basket of fresh-pulled roots still trailing soil, still faintly moving their tips.
Tallow candles drip from a chandelier made of antlers lashed together with catgut; their light falls warm and wavering across jars of teeth, pressed flowers, and one human shoe.
A pestle and mortar caked with dark residue sits beside a chopping block scored deep; around it, scattered seeds, shed claws, small bones, and one perfect unblemished white egg.
The window glass is thick and warped with age, letting in no daylight cleanly; pressed between the panes, flattened dried creatures — a frog, a bat, a hand-shaped leaf.
Copper instruments of unknown purpose hang from the walls alongside horseshoes, iron nails, shed snakeskin, a child's shoe filled with salt, and one enormous preserved deep-sea creature.
A trapdoor in the floor, padlocked shut, from beneath which roots emerge; around it, a ring of bird skulls, candle-stubs burned to nothing, and scattered red thread carefully knotted.
Every chair holds something: a sleeping black cat, a pile of feathers sorted by colour, a jar of cloudy water with something coiled inside, a doll with no face.
